entities.summary: John David Caputo is an American philosopher who is the Thomas J. Watson Professor of Religion Emeritus at Syracuse University and the David R. Cook Professor of Philosophy Emeritus at Villanova University. Caputo is a major figure associated with postmodern Christianity and continental philosophy of religion, as well as the founder of the theological movement known as weak theology. Much of Caputo's work focuses on hermeneutics, phenomenology, deconstruction, and theology. John D. Caputo was a philosophers & thinkers from Philadelphia (b. 1940-10-26, Philadelphia). A moderately significant entity in the historical record. Relevant to cause-and-effect analysis.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Caputo's work on weak theology has influenced contemporary debates in Christian theology and philosophy of religion, with implications for hermeneutics and phenomenology. His ideas have been taken up by scholars such as William T. Cavanaugh.
